ID.rec: Placement companies (P3MI) need a business licence (Art. 51, now under Law 6/2023, Art. 89A) and a Rp1.5 billion deposit (Art. 54(1)(b)), must resolve the problems of the workers they place (Art. 52(1)(c)) and stay responsible after revocation (Art. 58). Neither Law 18/2017 nor Government Regulation 59/2021 makes them jointly liable with the employer.
Law 18/2017 Arts. 51, 52, 54, 58, 74; Government Regulation 59/2021 · official text: https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/64508/uu-no-18-tahun-2017
ID.fees: Workers may not be charged placement costs (Art. 30(1)). BP2MI Regulation 9/2020 and its 2021 amendment were revoked by KP2MI Regulation 17/2025 (in force 26 August 2025): the employer now bears placement costs for all occupations by default (Art. 2(6)), but listed exceptions shift some costs to workers (Art. 3) and the Minister may set caps (Art. 6). Coded 1 because of the exceptions; arguably 2.
Law 18/2017 Art. 30; KP2MI (P2MI/BP2MI) Regulation 17/2025 Arts. 2, 3, 6, 9 · official text: https://jdih.bp2mi.go.id/index.php/Content/produk/8/889000625
ID.contract: A placement agreement and an employment contract with statutory minimum contents are required (Arts. 13(g)–(h), 15(2)); the contract is authenticated by an authorised official under KP2MI Regulation 3/2026 Art. 12(1), which replaced BP2MI Regulation 1/2020. Workers placed by a company for its own business are an exception (Art. 13(2)).
Law 18/2017 Arts. 13, 15; KP2MI Regulation 3/2026 Art. 12 · official text: https://jdih.bp2mi.go.id/index.php/Content/produk/8/889000772
ID.predep: Pre-departure orientation (OPP) is compulsory: placement companies must provide it (Government Regulation 59/2021 Arts. 1(11), 86(3)(k)), with provinces facilitating (Art. 59(c)). No legal text was found that makes it free to the worker: Law 18/2017 Art. 30 lists no costs and KP2MI Regulation 17/2025 does not mention OPP. Recoded from 2 to 1 on 13 November 2026.
ID.welfare: Social security membership is compulsory (Law 18/2017 Arts. 5(d), 29(1)); Minister of Manpower Regulation 4/2023 Art. 4(1) makes work-injury and death cover compulsory, including disability and repatriation; the State provides legal aid (Art. 21(1)(f)). KP2MI Regulation 9/2026 on social security now governs the same matter.
Law 18/2017 Arts. 5, 21, 29; Minister of Manpower Regulation 4/2023 · official text: https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/64508/uu-no-18-tahun-2017
ID.attache: The central government establishes labor attaché posts in destination countries chosen by placement numbers (Art. 22(1) and Elucidation).
ID.redress: Disputes go first to deliberation, then to the labor agencies and then to the courts (Art. 77); sanctions on companies under Arts. 58 and 74 and KP2MI Regulation 17/2025 Art. 8; restitution in criminal trafficking judgments (Law 21/2007 Art. 48). No specialized compensation body.
Law 18/2017 Arts. 58, 74, 77; Law 21/2007 Art. 48 · official text: https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/64508/uu-no-18-tahun-2017
ID.exit: Minimum age 18 (Art. 5(a)). Minister of Manpower Decision 260/2015, which halts placement with individual employers in 19 Middle Eastern countries, is in force and sex-neutral on its face, although it falls mainly on women domestic workers. The one-channel pilot (Decisions 291/2018 and 202/2023) was revoked by Decision 8/2026 (20 January 2026).
Law 18/2017 Art. 5; Minister of Manpower Decisions 260/2015 and 8/2026 · official text: https://jdih.kemnaker.go.id/peraturan/detail/618/keputusan-menteri-ketenagakerjaan-nomor-2
ID.return: District governments must carry out social and economic reintegration (Art. 41), with duties also at central and provincial level (Arts. 24, 42, 45, 47). KP2MI's role rests on the 2024 restructuring (Presidential Regulations 165/2024 and 166/2024).
PH.rec: Recruitment agencies are licensed by the Department of Migrant Workers and are jointly and severally liable with the employer for claims; corporate officers are personally liable.
RA 8042 s. 10 as amended by RA 10022 s. 7; RA 11641 s. 3(h) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116
PH.fees: The 2023 DMW Landbased Rules cap the placement fee at one month's basic salary and bar it for domestic workers and where the destination bars fees; the employer pays visa, airfare and government fees. Seafarers are governed by the 2026 Seabased Rules. The statute itself sets no amount (official guidance).
DMW Department Circular 01 s. 2023 ss. 56–59; DC 06 s. 2026 s. 54 · official guidance: https://dmw.gov.ph/archives/v1/resources/dsms/DMW/ISN-EXT/2023/DMW-DC-01-2023.pdf
PH.contract: Migrant Workers Offices verify contracts, and approval requires a joint-liability clause; standard contracts per type of hire are set by DMW rules.
RA 11641 s. 15(b); RA 8042 ss. 6(i), 10 · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/94035
PH.predep: Pre-employment and pre-departure orientation are mandatory under the DMW Landbased Rules (s. 169) and Seabased Rules (s. 202). The pre-employment seminar is free; pre-departure orientation may also be given by accredited private providers, so 'free of charge' is only partly established (official guidance).
DMW DC 01 s. 2023 s. 169; DC 06 s. 2026 s. 202 · official guidance: https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_DC_06_2026_188f50990f.pdf
PH.welfare: OWWA Fund with compulsory membership covering death, disability, repatriation and legal assistance; compulsory insurance for agency-hired workers at no cost to the worker.
RA 10801 ss. 4, 6(b), 8, 35; RA 8042 s. 37-A (RA 10022 s. 23) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/67104
PH.attache: Migrant Workers Offices are to be set up at all posts, as far as practicable, with priority for countries with many Filipino workers; they absorb the former POLO and OSWA.
PH.redress: Labor arbiters of the NLRC have original and exclusive jurisdiction over claims arising from overseas employment, with joint and several liability; the DMW adjudicates recruitment violations.
RA 8042 s. 10 as amended; RA 11641 ss. 8(j), 9(c) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116
PH.exit: The minimum age for household service workers is 23 for all genders (POEA GBR 2 s. 2007, lowering the 25 set in 2006; exemptions under GBR 4 s. 2011). Deployment to destinations can be restricted or banned (RA 8042 ss. 4–5; RA 11641 s. 8(k)); for Kuwait, deployment of first-time domestic workers has been deferred since 2023, and from 2024 only domestic workers with prior overseas experience may go (official guidance).
RA 8042 ss. 4–5; RA 11641 s. 8(k); POEA GBR 2 s. 2007; DMW MC 02 s. 2024 · official guidance: https://dmw.gov.ph/archives/poea/gbr/2007/2.pdf
PH.return: The National Reintegration Center for OFWs provides reintegration services and is now part of the DMW.
RA 8042 ss. 17–18 as amended by RA 10022 ss. 10–11; RA 11641 ss. 17, 19(e) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116
VN.rec: Service enterprises need a licence, charter capital of VND 5 billion and a deposit (Arts. 7(5), 10, 24); they compensate only damage they cause (Art. 26(2)(h)); the Law sets no joint liability with the employer. Law 22/2026 (from 1 March 2027) moves licence procedures to a decree.
VN.fees: Service fees are capped at one month's salary per 12 months, three months at most (Art. 23(4)(a)), and may be collected only after the supply contract is approved and the placement contract signed (Art. 23(2)(c)); brokerage may not be charged to workers (Art. 7(8)). Circular 09/2026 sets zero brokerage for Japan and zero service fees for some Japanese programs.
Law 69/2020 Arts. 7(8), 23; Circular 09/2026 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/
VN.contract: The supply contract has statutory minimum contents and needs prior Ministry approval (Arts. 19(2), 20(1)); the worker signs a written placement contract in the model form (Art. 21).
VN.predep: Orientation with a completion certificate is compulsory (Arts. 6(2)(c), 44(5), 65(2)) and covers rights and hotlines (Art. 65(1)); 74 periods under Circular 21/2021. The Law does not say who pays.
Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 44, 65; Circular 21/2021 Art. 12 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/
VN.welfare: The Overseas Employment Support Fund (Arts. 66–68) supports early return, abuse, disputes and death; under Decision 34/2025/QĐ-TTg (replacing Decision 40/2021, from 15 September 2025) it pays half of lawyer and court costs up to VND 50 million, VND 40 million on death and half the cost of repatriating remains. Social insurance also applies.
Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 66–68; Decision 34/2025/QĐ-TTg · official text: https://vbpl.vn/
VN.attache: The Ministry, with Foreign Affairs, posts officials to missions to manage workers abroad (Art. 70(2)(c)), and missions have statutory duties toward workers (Art. 71).
VN.redress: Complaints go to the authority, which can sanction enterprises and order refunds with interest and compensation for damage caused (Decree 283/2026 Art. 49, replacing Decree 12/2022 from 10 September 2026); this is a remedial order, not an adjudicating body, and other claims go to the courts.
Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 25, 69, 72; Decree 283/2026 Art. 49 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/
VN.exit: Minimum age 18 (Art. 3(1)); prohibited jobs and areas (Art. 7(12)–(13)) are sex-neutral on their face.
VN.return: The Ministry guides provinces, which may adopt support 'based on budget capacity'; employment service centers give labor-market information and enterprises help with job referral (Art. 60); psychosocial counseling is only encouraged (Art. 61). No public body has a duty to provide reintegration services. Recoded from 2 to 1 on 13 November 2026.
